text: Academic and technical comparisons show that China’s CLTC test procedure typically gives more optimistic range numbers than WLTP or EPA laboratory cycles, so CLTC‑reported ranges (including manufacturer 1,000 km claims) should be expected to overstate real‑world range versus WLTP/EPA metrics.

text: International bodies (IEA) forecast strong increases in China’s public charging capacity and a growing share of higher‑power public fast chargers up to 2030, supporting higher‑power charging access for premium vehicles in that timeframe.

text: Market forecasters (S&P Global Mobility and others) estimate Greater China cumulatively installing on the order of tens of millions of chargers by 2030 (S&P cited ~12.3 million chargers for Greater China in some forecasts), implying materially improved geographic access to charging for premium buyers across 2028–2031 (forecasts vary by provider and scenario).

text: (Inference) Combining vehicle‑level trends (wider 800‑1,000 V adoption; higher‑energy‑density cells entering premium cars) with charging‑side trends (wider roll‑out of 250–600 kW+ chargers and OEM megawatt pilots plus national charger targets) implies that premium mid‑size long‑wheelbase cars sold in China in 2028–2031 should be increasingly able to support much faster top‑up charging and longer practical ranges than 2024 models — but actual on‑road range will remain sensitive to test‑cycle (CLTC vs WLTP/EPA) differences and vehicle configuration.
